problem: VAL 43 / stuck on Veto loading screen after Nov 2025 patch - Bonjour / National Instruments mdns DLL conflict
symptoms: Game stuck on Riot/Veto loading screen (bar stuck ~10%) after a small patch
'There was an error connecting to the platform' VAL 43
Event Viewer Application log: VALORANT-Win64-Shipping.exe faulting module mdnsNSP.dll or nimdnsResponder.dll (exception 0xc0000005)
Client log: riot-messaging-service cannot resolve unconfigured.edge.rms.si.riotgames.com (OS error 11001)
root_causes: Apple Bonjour (mdnsNSP.dll) or National Instruments software (nimdnsResponder.dll) injected into the game process conflicts with the patched client

fixes.fix: Uninstall Bonjour (Apple) completely via Revo/Uninstalr, optionally run 'sfc /scannow' first, then uninstall Vanguard, let Riot Client reinstall it and reboot
Uninstall National Instruments software (and other apps shipping an mdns DLL)

Find the faulting module in Event Viewer (Windows Logs > Application, 'Faulting module name'), locate with 'dir /s /b C:\<file>', then 'takeown /f <path>' + 'icacls <path> /grant administrators:F' + 'del <path>' (System32 and SysWOW64 copies of nimdnsResponder.dll too; if access denied boot Safe Mode via msconfig > Boot > Safe boot > Minimal and delete there), then 'netsh winsock reset catalog' and reboot
ipconfig /flushdns; netsh winsock reset; netsh int ip reset; restart
Clean boot via msconfig (hide MS services, disable all, keep vgc) - reported not to help
Check vgc/vgk with 'sc query vgc/vgk'; sc config vgc start= auto, sc config vgk start= system, net start vgc/vgk - did not help one user
Upgrade Windows 10 to Windows 11 (single anecdote)

diagnostic_signals: Installed program list: Bonjour / Apple Bonjour Service
Event log Application: faulting module mdnsNSP.dll / nimdnsResponder.dll
Presence of mdnsNSP.dll / nimdnsResponder.dll in Program Files\Bonjour, System32, SysWOW64

problem: VAN-1 / Error 1067 - corrupted Vanguard (vgc/vgk) needing clean reinstall
symptoms: VAN-1 and Error 1067 on every launch

fixes.fix: Boot Safe Mode, delete C:\Program Files\Riot Vanguard, run as admin: reg delete HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\vgk /f and ...\vgc /f, reboot normally, launch Valorant so it reinstalls Vanguard
Follow the Vanguard 1067 thread steps (OP of a VAL 43 thread said this fixed it; steps were linked, not quoted)
Delete Vanguard via cmd, delete Vanguard folder, relaunch Valorant (user said it did not work; issue later fixed itself)
Reinstall Vanguard using Riot's Manual Uninstall guide (for BSOD)

diagnostic_signals: vgc/vgk service present and running (sc query vgc / vgk)
Event log service-start errors for vgk/vgc

problem: VAN-1 / UEFI Secure Boot verification failure with dual boot (Windows Boot Manager on another drive)
symptoms: VGC crashes with access violation 0xC0000005 in Event Viewer
'UEFI Secure Boot verification failure' despite Secure Boot enabled and latest BIOS
root_causes: Windows Boot Manager / EFI partition lives on the other OS drive or Linux bootloader is first in boot order, so Vanguard fails boot verification

fixes.fix: Install the Windows boot loader onto the Windows drive: shrink ~300MB on the Windows disk, disconnect the Linux drive, boot Windows install media > Repair > cmd, diskpart (list disk, select disk, create EFI partition) and rebuild BCD (guide author's multi-step procedure, tail not fully visible in data)
In BIOS boot order put Windows Boot Manager before Linux/GRUB

diagnostic_signals: Dual-boot detected (other OS entries in bcdedit / UEFI boot entries)
EFI system partition on a different disk than C:

problem: Secure Boot cannot be enabled / PC will not boot with Secure Boot on
symptoms: Secure Boot option does not stick after save
PC black screen or won't boot after enabling Secure Boot
Secure Boot key lists empty (PK/KEK/db: No Keys)
root_causes: Outdated BIOS with TPM/Secure Boot bugs
No Secure Boot keys installed (ASUS Key Management empty)

fixes.fix: Update the BIOS (install intermediate versions step by step if very old); user's 2017 BIOS had a TPM/Secure Boot bug fixed in newer BIOS
ASUS BIOS: Advanced > Security > Secure Boot Control = Enabled, open Key Management and install/update the default PK, KEK, db, dbx keys, save and verify
Disable CSM, ensure GPT/UEFI, enable Secure Boot (plus SVM for AMD)
Backup BIOS / short pins or clear CMOS if board stops booting after enabling Secure Boot
Downgrading to Windows 10 does not avoid the requirement

diagnostic_signals: msinfo32 BIOS Mode (UEFI vs Legacy) and Secure Boot State
Get-Disk partition style GPT vs MBR

problem: Vanguard says UEFI Secure Boot required even though it is enabled
symptoms: Game closes after a few minutes with 'requires UEFI secure boot'
msinfo32 shows Secure Boot disabled though BIOS says enabled
VAN RESTRICTION requiring Secure Boot and HVCI
root_causes: Secure Boot state not properly applied (needs toggle)

fixes.fix: BIOS: set Secure Boot to Disabled, save, then re-enable it and save again (also redo CSM/UEFI settings)
Fully remove Valorant/Riot/Vanguard with Revo Uninstaller and reinstall (OP said did not fix)
Check msinfo32 for actual Secure Boot State; wait and re-check since it may flag later

problem: HVCI / Memory Integrity will not turn on or stay on (BSOD on reboot)
symptoms: Memory integrity turns on in UI but reverts after reboot with BSOD
VAN restriction requiring HVCI after Windows update
root_causes: Leftover BIOS settings from Windows 10 era

fixes.fix: Reset BIOS to defaults, then re-enable SVM/virtualization, TPM, Secure Boot
Enable AMD SVM / Intel VT-x in BIOS; remove incompatible drivers listed by Memory Integrity

diagnostic_signals: Incompatible driver list from Core isolation

problem: VAN IOMMU restriction - muted audio or BSOD loop
symptoms: 'IOMMU restriction is in place, restart required'
PC audio muted after launching Valorant until reboot
PCIe sound card disabled by Vanguard
root_causes: Vanguard IOMMU/DMA protection conflicts with audio/WiFi drivers or PCIe cards

fixes.fix: Upgrade to Windows 11 (fixed it), but reinstalling the WiFi card driver brought it back; run on Ethernet
Install audio drivers from hardware vendor site, create a new sound output and set it as default (user unsure which step helped)
Reinstall updated audio driver, remove sound enhancements, update BIOS; enable IOMMU/SVM/TPM/Memory Integrity/Secure Boot

diagnostic_signals: PCIe sound card present (e.g. Creative AE-5)

symptoms: Cannot get TPM 2.0 on HP ProDesk 600 G1

fixes.fix: External TPM 2.0 module (uncertain it works)

problem: Performance collapse (CPU limited to ~800 MHz) after BIOS changes for Secure Boot/TPM
symptoms: 80-100% CPU usage with 14-40 FPS after BIOS edits
root_causes: BIOS changes capped CPU frequency at 800 MHz

fixes.fix: Revert BIOS setting that limited CPU (OP fixed it, exact setting not specified)

diagnostic_signals: Current CPU clock vs max (Win32_Processor CurrentClockSpeed vs MaxClockSpeed)

problem: Periodic stutter / FPS drops fixed by disabling Realtek 2.5GbE / Ethernet or Wi-Fi adapter (Vanguard + Realtek conflict)
symptoms: Stutter when enemies appear or shooting
Whole PC freeze with rt640x64 NDIS adapter resetting events
root_causes: Realtek 2.5GbE / PCIe GbE driver conflicts with Vanguard (NDIS/power-saving bug), mostly on new AM5 boards with RTX 50 / 9800X3D

fixes.fix: Device Manager > Network adapters: disable Realtek Gaming 2.5GbE / Ethernet Family Controller if on Wi-Fi (or disable Wi-Fi adapter if on Ethernet); disable Bluetooth if unused
Install Realtek NDIS configuration fixer 'Auto Installation Program (NDIS) Not Support Power saving' version
Disable Windows Fast Startup (stopped freeze for one user)
Uninstall Realtek adapter in Device Manager and reboot to reinstall driver (fixed high ping after USB light)

diagnostic_signals: Network adapters present: Realtek 2.5GbE / PCIe GbE

problem: FPS drops with Discord (or other overlays) enabled
symptoms: FPS falls to 80-100 whenever something happens
Frame drops when enemies appear only with Discord open
root_causes: Discord overlay (and others) interfering after patch

fixes.fix: Disable Discord overlay (it had re-enabled itself)
Disable overlays in general
Uninstall the Microsoft input component (OP said uninstalling 'microsoft input' fixed it)

diagnostic_signals: Running processes: Discord (overlay), GeForce Overlay, Xbox Game Bar, Steam overlay
Overlay hooks loaded into VALORANT process

problem: Low GPU usage / FPS drops after UE5 patch on laptops and new PCs (power plan, wrong GPU, Nvidia profile, drivers)
root_causes: Game on iGPU instead of dGPU
V-sync/frame cap in NVIDIA app profile

fixes.fix: Turn off V-Sync, in NVIDIA app set Valorant max frame rate, make sure it runs on the RTX GPU not iGPU; follow AMDHelp guide steps 9, 10, 11-NV
Follow community optimization guide (r/AMDHelp) steps 1-7, 9, 10, 11-NV, 12, 14; check controller section
Update or clean install GPU driver (NVIDIA 581.80/581.94 beta or hotfix), DDU if Windows Update installed a driver
Set graphics quality to High to raise GPU usage; Process Lasso for permanent priority/affinity
Clean DirectX/shader cache

diagnostic_signals: GPU in use by VALORANT process (iGPU vs dGPU)
Windows power plan and plugged-in state

problem: Intel laptop freeze / stuck loading in fullscreen (outdated Intel graphics driver)
symptoms: Game freezes or stuck on loading in fullscreen, works in windowed

fixes.fix: Update Intel Graphics driver (Intel Driver Assistant / newer September package)

problem: Windows 11 24H2 / floaty, inconsistent mouse aim
symptoms: Floaty or delayed mouse, flicks not landing, micro-stutter after Windows update or clean install
root_causes: GPU scheduling/timers behavior in 24H2; Windows 'optimizations for windowed games'

fixes.fix: Turn off Windows Graphics setting 'Optimizations for windowed games' (fixed mouse for OP)
RTSS frame cap at (refresh multiple - 1), e.g. 479, application detection High, Scanline Sync 0; disable HAGS; restart
Turn off Reflex, NVIDIA low latency, VRR/G-Sync as testing options

problem: Standby memory fill causing stutter
symptoms: Game fine initially, stutters after minutes

fixes.fix: Run ISLC (Wagnardsoft) as admin, 'Free memory is lower than' = half of RAM, 1000ms polling, start with Windows
Check Resource Monitor free vs standby memory
